title: fix(chat): completed replies stay busy after delayed updates

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes: chat stays busy and subsequent messages remain queued when a completed response is followed by delayed transcript updates.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: completed replies return the composer to Send, and queued messages resume in order without duplicate responses or a Gateway update.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

Keep transcript reconciliation separate from live turn admission. The existing conversation-state owner now commits assistant content, usage and finalization atomically before publication, rather than splitting those changes across provider callbacks. Completed runs cannot restart through delayed output or replayed starts.

Preserve newer turns, explicit finals received before send acknowledgment, retained tool results/review outcomes, and main's newly landed rich-content presentation. No timeout, forced-idle workaround, automatic abort or queue bypass is added.

The original regressions failed before the fix. Follow-up review found two additional event-order bugs; both were reproduced and repaired. Integration with current main also preserves runless/legacy tool pairing and late review outcomes. The current candidate has 779 passing focused provider/reducer/runtime/streaming tests.

Independent implementation and proof-plan review used Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra through the available `code-review` role (`rubber-duck` is not exposed by the host). Both reviewers rechecked the integration repairs and reported no remaining actionable finding in that delta. A current-head compiled parser/provider replay passes all 14 cases. Full local closeout and the six mounted Debug/unsigned-Release cases passed; required CI remains the merge gate.

Managed tests use an isolated tray-data override and clear inherited integration/GPU/MXC/E2E opt-ins. The signed cleanup-host default correctly rejected the initial ordinary Release attempt. The later Release command uses the documented non-published local test mode from `docs/RELEASING.md`, also used by PR release smoke; it does not weaken signed publication requirements.

The native command below passed 3/3 cases against the Debug app and 3/3 against the unsigned local Release app, with no skipped selected cases. Both app binaries are stamped with the candidate SHA; the existing UI test runner is reused.

An earlier integrated full Shared run hit the unchanged file-worker locked-cleanup test. Its four focused cases passed on diagnosis; the current-head full rerun is recorded separately above rather than hiding that attempt.

## Real Behavior Proof

<!--
Paste at least one current-head proof item that directly demonstrates the
changed behavior. Use copied live output, screenshots or video, UI diagnostics,
`winnode` output, raw MCP JSON-RPC, gateway invoke output, redacted runtime
logs, or linked artifacts.
-->

- Environment tested: native Windows ARM64, isolated Companion profile, fixture Gateway, synthetic data only. No real Gateway or live user profile was used for application proof.
- PR head or commit tested: `da309a81e43966ddbbb51d53408d78a89d06c07f`; compiled parser/provider replay and mounted Debug/unsigned-Release app proof use this commit.
- Exact steps or command run: enable `OPENCLAW_RUN_GATEWAY_FIXTURE_UI=1`, keep `OPENCLAW_RUN_KEYBOARD_PROOF=0`, and bind `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_FIXTURE_APP` to the explicit candidate executable. Run `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Tray.UITests\OpenClaw.Tray.UITests.csproj -c Debug -r win-arm64 -p:Platform=ARM64 -p:DevBuild=false --no-build --no-restore --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~CompletedRunLateSnapshotLeavesNativeComposerReadyAndQueueDraining|FullyQualifiedName~BackgroundMediaRetransmitAndRetainedToolOutcomePreserveNewerNativeTurn'`. Repeat with the unsigned Release app; the already-built UI runner is reused, while the app under test changes.
- Evidence after fix: the fixture drives lifecycle end, delayed persisted snapshot (with and without run ID), and final; asserts native Send rather than Stop, no Working row, one completed answer, and queued follow-ups sent exactly once. A separate case preserves newer-turn streaming and its media while older retained output is repaired.
- Observed result: current-head compiled parser/provider replay passed 14/14 cases. For end -> runless snapshot -> final, the final observation is `TurnActive=false`, one assistant entry, no streaming assistant; the follow-up reaches the bridge once with an empty queue. Both mounted builds passed all three selected cases: native Send returned, the Working row disappeared, the final reply appeared once, and three sends completed in order with queue count zero. Captures were inspected; all owned fixture processes closed afterward.
- Screenshot or artifact links verified? (`Yes`/`No`/`N/A`): N/A. Current-head copied observations and test results are included here; local captures are not represented as public artifact links.
- Not verified or blocked: real Gateway/provider behavior, signed Release publication, installer lifecycle and native x64 desktop proof are not claimed. Required hosted CI must pass before merge.
